Definition: from G5384 and G2462; fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four men in the New Testament:--Philip.
BiblicalUsage: Philippos is Philip, and the name belongs to four men in the New Testament, chiefly the apostle and the evangelist. Jesus finds Philip and says, Follow Me, and Philip finds Nathanael and says, Come and see, and later Jesus tests him at the feeding of the five thousand, asking where they shall buy bread. The other Philip, the evangelist, is sent to the desert road to meet the Ethiopian eunuch.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two Philips show me two kinds of following: the apostle who brings his friend to Jesus, and the evangelist who runs to a stranger's chariot. Their lives are on their profiles; here the name covers both, because both answered when they were called.
